Abandoned results cannot authorize or answer another revive. The blocking worker owns only a tmux Arc and a runtime handle and performs one pane read; it has no registry, caller, or revive continuation (crates/daemon/src/http/revive.rs:380-393). Dropping the timed-out join handle detaches that work, and its eventual result is discarded. Existing per-command reply channels, serialized enqueue/write, one FIFO waiter consumed per reply, and original-client Arc checks preserve command/replacement correlation (crates/tmux/src/control.rs:245-281,383-419,444-462).

The wait's read is launch-free: list_panes_without_launch calls query_live, which passes may_start=false and does not start/restart a control client (crates/tmux/src/lib.rs:1114-1119; crates/tmux/src/control.rs:233-294). Caveat: abandoned reads are not absolutely free of all shared-state effects. Existing error cleanup may clear control-client bookkeeping and kill/reap the original control client (control.rs:171-175,289-291,383-393). This does not mutate seat registry or authority; the original-client Arc check prevents an old timeout from clearing a replacement client.

Unknown/error/deadline ends the helper; it does not supply launch permission. Lock acquisition, registry reread, and the fresh authoritative observation follow independently (revive.rs:342-393,441-450). The unchanged locked decision refuses active processes and present or unverifiable panes (revive.rs:585-593); evidence requirements and parent/prime override authorization remain unchanged (revive.rs:404-415,594-639). Policy versus brake remains unchanged: the process observation decides eligibility; a present or unverifiable pane vetoes launch.

C34 follow-up R275-FU-01, not a final-round block: blocking-read lifecycle. Reads are sequential, with at most one unfinished worker per abandoned helper invocation, but the three-second REPLY_TIMEOUT bounds reply reception only. It does NOT bound mutex acquisition, pipe writes, or child reaping (control.rs:245-291,397-410,171-175). Started spawn_blocking tasks are non-cancellable; repeated timed-out invocations can therefore accumulate workers under a stuck control path. Do not describe the entire worker lifetime as unconditionally bounded by three seconds. No normal-use security-impacting regression was identified under C33. Whole-worker admission/cancellation hardening belongs to follow-up; the correctness reviewer has been notified. Timing-witness scaling is separately a C34 follow-up owned by correctness.

Complete added-line inspection found no new secrets, C21 private-home paths, or credential/home-read operations. This is a delta review, not a history-wide secret scan.
